title: Computational Design and Provisional Novelty Assessment of Three Site-Specific Phytochemical Glycoside Analogues for Inflammatory Skin Disease
content: Paeoniflorin, glycyrrhizin and hesperidin are structurally defined glycosides with experimental links to epithelial inflammation, yet their high polarity, microstate complexity and matrix-dependent exposure constrain direct translation. This computational hypothesis study proposes three site-specific analogues: paeoniflorin 6′-O-[(3-fluorooxetan-3-yl)methyl] carbonate (AIIP-PAE-FOX-001), glycyrrhizin C30 2-(3,3-difluoroazetidin-1-yl)ethyl ester (AIIP-GLY-DFA-001), and hesperidin 3′-O-[2-(2-oxa-6-azaspiro[3.3]heptan-6-yl)ethyl] ether (AIIP-HES-OAS-001). Their molecular graphs were constructed from PubChem parent structures, canonicalized with RDKit 2026.09.1 and checked by computational recovery of each parental InChIKey. On 16 October 2026, the neutral candidate structures returned no records in the tested PubChem, ChEMBL and ChEBI identity modalities, whereas all parent controls returned records. Exact-name and motif-focused public web and patent searches identified no individualized match, although related site modifications and generic heterocycle prior art were found. The completed work is limited to molecular-structure definition, graph-derived physicochemical descriptors, structure-based microstate and conformational considerations, and a dated public-registry and prior-art audit. The descriptor values are in silico estimates rather than measurements; no molecular-dynamics or experimental solution-state conformational study was performed. No candidate was synthesized, isolated, analytically characterized or subjected to experimental physicochemical or biological testing. The predicted differences therefore do not demonstrate a physicochemical advantage. AIIP-PAE-FOX-001 is prioritized for initial experimental evaluation because it is the lowest-molecular-weight, non-amine candidate and has precedent for modification at the selected 6′ site. A minimum validation package should include synthesis, positional assignment by high-resolution mass spectrometry and one- and two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, chromatographic purity, equilibrium solubility, an appropriate pH-dependent partition measurement, and chemical and esterase stability relative to paeoniflorin. A physicochemical advantage would require a higher recoverable intact free concentration or improved stability in the intended matrix, not a calculated cLogP change alone. Biological validation remains a subsequent stage. The present results support only provisional public-registry novelty, not universal novelty, patentability, synthesis, activity or regulatory new-chemical-entity status.
